question: Can Roque et al.'s 2022 Bagac River fish assemblage paper provide a bounded, reusable historical source for the Central Luzon research ledger?

source.citation: Roque, N. B. C., Manliclic, A. D. C., & Corpuz, M. N. C. (2022). Key environmental and habitat variables affecting the fish assemblages in Bagac River systems, Bataan, Philippines. AACL Bioflux, 15(6), 2870–2880.
source.licenseEvidence: The publisher PDF identifies the article as open access under the Creative Commons Attribution License and requires source/author credit.
source.accessNote: The official publisher PDF text was reviewed through its indexed document view. A direct local download attempt failed at the host, so no local PDF copy or SHA-256 is claimed.

studyScope.sourceReportedWaterbodyContext: The paper describes the Bagac River system on Mount Mariveles, flowing from springs and highland runoff through tributaries toward the West Philippine Sea. This downstream connection does not make every reach marine or brackish.
studyScope.surveyDesign: Nine stations across upstream, midstream, and downstream sections; each section included three longitudinal sub-sections of about 60 m. The paper describes backpack electrofishing, hand nets, daytime sampling of about 30 minutes, and environmental measurements.
studyScope.fieldDateLimit: No exact fish-collection calendar date or species-by-date table was found in the reviewed source text. Publication and acceptance dates are not collection dates.
studyScope.identityLimit: The methods say organisms were identified to the lowest possible taxon using literature; the paper does not provide a specimen-by-name voucher/catalog crosswalk in the reviewed text. Some native/juvenile fish were released after in-situ identification, so preserved material does not cover every fish assertion.

systematicReviewCrosswalk.secondaryLead: Baron and Garces (2026), Table 2, lists a Bagac River row as Roque et al. 2019 with 17 fish taxa and five goby taxa; Bagac does not appear in that article's Table 1 publication list.
systematicReviewCrosswalk.primaryPaperComparison: The accessible 2022 Bagac article reports 15 fish taxa. The distinct 2019 conference paper is now identified and its primary table lists 17 source taxa, including five Gobiidae taxa, matching the synthesis's 2019 row.
systematicReviewCrosswalk.decision: Keep the 2019 conference paper and 2022 article as separate source records. The field dates and possible sample overlap are not resolved; do not combine their totals or rows. The synthesis's omission from Table 1 and study-row denominator conflict remain open.

qualityAndUseLimits: The reported 400 are study specimens, not river-wide abundance or a current fishery estimate.
Section-level representative coordinates in the paper do not locate individual fish captures or all nine stations; no fish point geometry is added.
The article reports a small downstream salinity measurement and mangrove patches, but does not support assigning one salinity class to the whole river.
No item-specific field dates, specimen accession list, full voucher-to-taxon crosswalk, or independent name review was completed in this source screen.
The paper's ecological or water-quality discussion is not current fishing-safety advice, legal guidance, catchability information, or a diet source.

imageReview.figureAssessment: The article's Figure 1 is a locality/river-section map, not a fish portrait. No taxon-identified fish profile photo was approved.
imageReview.decision: No image was copied, cropped, registered, or added to the app; fish without independently cleared media retain the species-photo fallback.

nextAction: Keep this 2022 paper distinct from the identified 2019 Bagac conference paper and later Bataan surveys. Continue resolving taxonomy, field dates, possible sample overlap, and the remaining Central Luzon waterbody inventory.

sources.supports: Primary paper citation, methods, reported sites, 400-specimen/15-taxon abstract summary, waterbody context, and CC BY license statement.
Publisher issue listing and article citation.
Secondary Table 1/Table 2 citation mismatch noted only as a discovery crosswalk.
The distinct 2019 author-uploaded primary source and its 17-taxon/five-Gobiidae summary; reuse remains unverified.
